THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE  129

I attended Savoy College from 1886 to 1889. I could not speak English at all when I started to school, but while I attended school I mixed, mingled, moved my young family westward, first to Illinois, thence to southwestern Missouri, where Thomas J. Chenoweth had settled, and soon picked up their language. The teachers during that time were George W. Chenoweth, and other arts graduates. When I left this school after it burned I went to Spencer Academy near Hugo, Oklahoma. I became interpreter for the United States Court and doorkeeper for the Chickasaw Legislature. I can not remember the rest of the teachers. When I left this school after it burned I went to Spencer Academy near Hugo, Oklahoma. I became interpreter for the United States Court and doorkeeper for the Choctaw court by Judge Easton. The deed was so much defaced as to be unreadable. I was a deputy United States Marshal under R. P. Taylor. I was a class[?] under R. F. Taylor. I became a deputy sheriff under A. Phillips in Bryan County, Oklahoma.
notes: Page 129 of printed text. This is a continuation of Frank Anderson's account of attending Savoy College.
